summary:
What is our project? Astro Band has two parts that work together. The first is a wrist-worn band. It is our proposed design for a health sensor, and it is deliberately not a watch. It keeps track of heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, blood pressure, stress, sleep and radiation dose. The second is HALO, a voice assistant. When a reading drifts, or the astronaut simply says they do not feel well, HALO starts a conversation. It asks what is wrong, asks how severe it is on a scale of one to ten, and then guides them through a treatment one step at a time. A headache, for example, becomes a short checklist with timers: check the air, drink water, relax the neck, rest. The app also has a ground station panel. It sends alerts to Mission Control and the flight surgeon, flags the medical facility when something critical happens, and handles the case where contact is lost.


2.Why does it matter? Missions to the Moon and Mars will take crews much farther from home than the space station does. Messages take longer to travel, help cannot always answer right away, and the crew has to look after itself more than ever before. NASA's Human Research Program groups the health risks of spaceflight into five hazards. Many of them build up slowly and are easy to miss without constant monitoring.
details: The challenge asks for a way to monitor astronaut health. We built the answer around three ideas. • Continuous monitoring. The band classifies every reading as Normal, Watch or Alert. Five live hazard cards, one for each NASA hazard, update from the same data so the crew and the ground team see the whole picture at a glance.Independence when Earth is far away. HALO does not wait for a delayed reply. It gives guided steps right away, and the app can simulate the signal delay for the station (about 0.5 seconds), the Moon (1.3 seconds) and Mars (4 to 24 minutes). • A safety net to the ground. Critical alerts go to Mission Control with a medical facility warning. If the link drops, alerts are stored on the band, the ground station raises a "crew contact lost" alert after a short time, and everything is sent as soon as the link comes back
